questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the service configuration management practice in ITIL 4?
options: To ensure accurate, reliable information about the configuration of services and their CIs is available when and where it is needed
To replace the incident management practice entirely
To track only the financial cost of IT hardware
To schedule when changes are allowed to go live
questions.explain: The practice is about trustworthy information being available at the point of need, not just storing data for its own sake.

questions.q: Which of these could legitimately be treated as a configuration item (CI)?
options: Only physical servers and network hardware
A disaster recovery runbook, an on-call role, an application, and a server — any of them, if losing track of it puts a service at risk
Only items that appear on a financial asset register
Only software, never documentation or roles
questions.explain: ITIL 4's test for a CI is whether it needs to be managed to deliver a service, not what category of thing it is.

questions.q: Why do CI relationships matter more than just having a list of CIs?
options: Relationships are optional and mostly decorative in a CMDB
A list of CIs with no relationships is already enough for root-cause investigation
Relationships turn a flat inventory into a graph you can use for impact analysis and root-cause investigation
Relationships only matter for the change enablement practice
questions.explain: The relationship graph is what lets you trace from a failing component to everything it affects, or from a recurring incident back to a shared cause.

questions.q: Which Chapter 4 practice relies on configuration data to assess the blast radius of a proposed change before approving it?
options: Service desk
Change enablement
Knowledge management
Service level management
questions.explain: Change enablement consumes the CI relationship graph to understand what else a proposed change might affect.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is intentionally left for a later, dedicated course in this ServiceNow path?
options: The basic definition of what a configuration item is
The deep implementation detail of ServiceNow's CMDB and its Common Service Data Model (CSDM)
The purpose statement of the configuration management practice
The relationship between configuration management and incident management
questions.explain: This lesson introduces the practice conceptually; ServiceNow's specific CMDB and CSDM implementation gets its own course later in the path.
